You are a clinical information extraction system. Read ONE outpatient consultation transcript (lines like "[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): text") and return ONE JSON object with the clinical information it contains, in the trained clinical-extraction format. Return only the JSON.

Rules
- Use only what is said. Never invent or infer. Leave out every field and section that has no information.
- Record who said it (doctor, patient, nurse, caregiver, family_member, clinical_staff, unknown), in lower case.
- A denied finding goes in negative_findings, never in symptoms. A doctor's question is not a fact: use the answer.
- A medicine the patient takes is not an allergy. A stopped medicine is not current. Dose, frequency, route and indication belong only to the medicine they were said for.
- Doctor impressions are provisional or differential, and only if the doctor stated one. Do not add a diagnosis the doctor declined to give.
- Use the right status for plan items (planned, completed, recommended, conditional). Do not add a follow-up that was not arranged.
- If speakers disagree or a detail is unclear (dose, date, allergy, name), keep both statements and describe the real doubt in clinical_uncertainties.
- Cite one or two segment ids per item in evidence_ids. clinical_evidence is []. All confidence fields are null.

Transcript (encounter 00001)
[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi, doctor. Long queue outside, but here I am.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine, sit down. So, what brings you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, so... stiffness in the morning. That's why I came.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it begin?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): For three weeks, I'd say.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): It happens once or twice a day. Moderate, really. A neighbour of mine said I should see someone about it.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's get your blood pressure and the other basics.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): almost there..
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: blood pressure 120 over 76, SpO2 99 percent on room air. And temp 36.6 degrees, pulse 72.
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that that okay?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay, we'll put it in context in a moment
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): shall we do the examination?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): fine
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me press here.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's mild swelling on the right knee, and a grating feel when I bend it.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay, good, that's the examination any fever, redness over the knee or back pain at all?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none of those.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): any pins and needles or loss of strength anywhere?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): no, nothing like that
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, what do you do for work?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): I work in an office, mostly sitting at a desk
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you get any exercise?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): I walk for about half an hour most days
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you living with family?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): I stay with my daughter and her family.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): are you on any regular medication?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing, no.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): right, any surgery in your history?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Just a hernia repair, about five years back.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): do you have any medical conditions I should know about?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I've never had anything serious.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): so where does that leave us? I think we're dealing with osteoarthritis of the knees at this stage
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's get blood tests, for joint pain.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): okay, noted
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's use etoricoxib, 60 milligrams, once a day, for five days. It's for knee pain. Losing even a few kilos takes a lot of load off the knees, and I'd like you to do the strengthening exercises. I'll also refer you to physiotherapy.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): okay
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep an eye out, and if the symptoms get worse, call us the same day or go to emergency.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): okay, I'll remember
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's it on my side. Anything unclear?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): thanks, that was helpful

[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hello, come through.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): evening, doctor
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): What made you decide to come in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): So, I've been feeling a bit dizzy after taking all my tablets, doctor.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's go through your medication. What are you taking?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastatin, 20 milligrams, at night. It's metformin, 500 milligrams, twice a day for my sugar. Though honestly, some days I forget to take it. Aspirin, 75 milligrams, once a day
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): since when have you been taking it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): For two months.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): right, when did it begin?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, so it's been like this since Monday.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): How bad is it, would you say?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I, I'd give it a seven, out of ten.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): have you had dry mouth?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, actually.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): How intense does it get?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mild, really.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): And And then?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been feeling confused about which tablets to take too. Yeah, I did have an upset stomach at one point, but that's gone now
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): So, a few quick ones: vomiting, black stools or fainting?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of those.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): let me check a few things. Any falls, low mood or chest pain?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no falls, low mood or chest pain.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is your urine normal, no changes?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No changes there.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you have any known allergies at all?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I think I reacted to some antibiotic once, years ago. I don't remember which one, or what happened exactly.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you ever been under the knife?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I had a stent put in my heart, two years ago.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Now some background about your lifestyle.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I gave up drinking about three years ago. I used to smoke but I quit five years ago. I'm a software engineer, so I'm at a screen all day. Yes, I live on my own.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about family history, any illnesses that run in the family?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): my father had kidney stones my mother has migraines
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about your general health, any conditions you're being treated for?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): High cholesterol, for two years. I kept putting it off, which I know isn't sensible. I took the morning off to come in today. I have diabetes, for about a year. I thought it would sort itself out, but it hasn't. I've never really been one for hospitals. I've got heart disease.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): okay, I can see diabetes in your file as well i'll take a few measurements first
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Almost there...
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay: respiratory rate 16, temperature 36.8, pulse is 65 beats a minute, oxygen saturation is 97 percent, BP is 125 over 74. Stop me if I've got anything wrong. You've been feeling a bit dizzy after taking all your tablets, since Monday, and no chest pain or low mood.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): mm, um, that's right
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): An ECG is what I'd like next, for dizziness. I think blood tests makes sense here, for medication review. Bring every box and bottle you have at home to the next visit, even the herbal ones, and we'll sort them together. Call the clinic if you need us.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No questions. Thank you.

Transcript (encounter 00003)
[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good evening, um, doctor, thank you for staying late.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine, sit down. So, what brings you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I've been dealing with more breathlessness than usual
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have you had it?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Ten days, I think... sorry, about four days, I got that wrong.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, give me more detail on it, whatever comes to mind.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, stairs. That makes it it worse. It's every other day. I get some relief from resting.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, any poor sleep because of the cough as well?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, I have. About poor sleep because of the cough, honestly, a couple of times a week. Oh, and a rattling chest. Hmm, as for rattling chest, it feels mild to me.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And swollen ankles, any of that?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No swollen ankles.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what about weight loss, chest pain or coughing up blood?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): I haven't had weight loss, chest pain or coughing up blood, no
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): On the cardiac side, anything I should know?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing with my heart.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are there any allergies on your record that I should check?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, eggs. I've no idea what the reaction was, only that I'm not supposed to have it.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do your parents or siblings have any long-term illnesses?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had kidney stones.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, what about your general health, any conditions you're being treated for?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I've had COPD for two years now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medication at the moment, including things from the pharmacy?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Tiotropium inhaler, once a day for my chest.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): tell me about your routine, work, habits, that sort of thing
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Barely, I'm mostly sedentary these days. I run a small shop, so I'm on my feet a lot. I live with my family, my husband and two kids.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll check your pressure and pulse.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): hold still for me..
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: saturation 90 percent, temperature is 37.0 degrees. And blood pressure 142 over 72, weight 80 kilos, respiratory rate 22, height 162 centimetres, pulse 93.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come over here and I'll have a look.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me press here.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Air entry is reduced on both sides with a prolonged breathing out phase.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): thanks, please take a seat again. Having listened and examined, this looks most like a flare-up of COPD. I'd like to arrange blood tests for infective exacerbation. For this, prednisolone, 30 milligrams, once a day, for five days. You take it by mouth. That's for COPD flare-up. I'm prescribing doxycycline, 100 milligrams, twice a day, for five days. That's for chest infection. Please take the tablets with food so they don't upset your stomach
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do get help quickly if you become more breathless or your lips turn blue.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, I understand.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll want another look in one week okay, we're done for today take care
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): No questions. Thank you.

[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): It's been about two weeks, I'm fairly sure.

[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, it's... hard to say, it's kind of... I don't know—

[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Pretty severe, if I'm being honest.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything that tends to go along with it?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): When it starts I tend to get breathlessness on exertion as well.
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): I was just going to say that the main thing is—
[SEG0014] person_3 (NURSE): Sorry to cut in, doctor, quick question: shall I bring the trolley in now or later?
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Later, thanks. Please go on. Have you had tiredness?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, actually. Um, um, the breathlessness on exertion? That's been for three weeks.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): A four out of ten, I suppose. Resting helps a bit.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you get pain at rest or fever?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, um, no pain at rest, no fever. I was sweating with it at one point, but that went away on its own.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, and what about swelling in the ankles, fainting, palpitations or cough?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling in the ankles, fainting, palpitations or cough, none of it.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any rashes or skin problems otherwise?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): No, skin's been fine.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything unusual with passing urine?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing there, no.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there anything medical in your background?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): I have high blood pressure, for about a year.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): I see.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): I have diabetes, for nearly five years. I've had high cholesterol, yes. I've got heart disease.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so diabetes and high cholesterol are already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, what medicines do you take regularly?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Telmisartan, 40 milligrams, maybe, once a day for my pressure.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, did you happen to bring the box or the paperwork?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): No, it's at home. Glycomet. I take it 500 milligrams, twice a day. Though honestly, some days I forget to take it. Aspirin. I take it 75 milligrams, once a day.
[SEG0036] person_3 (NURSE): Doctor, our chart from the last visit lists it as 150 milligrams.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Do you happen to have the current prescription here?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I left it at home.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family with similar problems or other conditions?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother has migraines.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you have any known allergies at all?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing I'm aware of.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any previous surgeries?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, I had my tonsils out, when I was a child.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now some background about your lifestyle.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't drink at all. I walk for about half an hour most days. I try to avoid too much sugar.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me examine, it won't take long.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at this properly.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear and there's no swelling in your ankles.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): A little pressure here, tell me if it's tender.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds are normal, no murmurs.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's all I need, thank you. Let me tell you where I've got to. My working impression is angina-type chest pain. You've had tightness in your chest when you walk for about two weeks, severe, and no cough or pain at rest.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, that's right.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order an echocardiogram, for chest tightness.
[SEG0056] person_4 (CLINICAL_STAFF): The earliest is Friday, 10 am.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order a lipid profile, for cardiovascular risk.
[SEG0058] person_3 (NURSE): Doctor, I did an ECG before they came in, the result's on your screen.
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, thank you. The treatment will be atorvastatin, 40 milligrams, at night, long term. You take it by mouth. That's for cardiovascular risk. For this, GTN spray, 0.4 milligrams, when the chest tightness comes, as needed. That should help with chest tightness. Don't push through the chest tightness, stop, sit down, and use the spray if I've given it to you.
[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): Make sure you're drinking plenty of fluids, two to three litres a day if you can, and get proper rest. A cardiologist would be the right next step, I'll refer you. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose. Let's hold off on a treadmill test for now, and if there's no change in two weeks we can revisit it.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do get help quickly if the chest tightness comes at rest or lasts more than fifteen minutes.
[SEG0062] person_1 (PATIENT): Understood.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ask me anything before you go.
[SEG0064] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing more from me, you know, thanks.

[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, noted.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, can I examine you now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll go gently.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's a small external pile at the edge, and I don't see any fissure.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Almost done with this part.

[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, that's the examination. Have you had any fever?
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Um, actually, doctor, I did notice fever. He doesn't always say.
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): No, I don't think I did. Maybe a little, I'm not sure.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'll note both what you've said and what you've noticed. Okay, did you get change in bowel habit, family history of bowel cancer or black stools?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): No. None of those.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss or abdominal pain at all?
[SEG0023] person_4 (PATIENT): No, no weight loss or abdominal pain.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything on the skin I should know about?
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): No rashes.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about allergies, to medicines or foods or anything else?
[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): I was told I'm allergic to latex, but I don't remember what reaction I had.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, what medicines do you take regularly?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He is on iron tablets, once a day, I give it to him. He is on sertraline, 50 milligrams, once a day for my mood, I give it to him.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): And for how long?
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Nearly five years now.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you live alone?
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, I live on my own.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you have a job?
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): I'm a self-employed electrician.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you got any chronic problems?

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood.
[SEG0039] person_4 (PATIENT): I've got depression.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so depression is already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today. Have you had any previous surgeries?
[SEG0041] person_4 (PATIENT): No operations, no.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, is there a family history of anything significant?
[SEG0043] person_4 (PATIENT): My mother has diabetes. My mother had high blood pressure.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, so my impression is this: This looks most like haemorrhoids. I want to be honest that this is an impression, not a final answer. I'd also keep something higher up in the bowel that we shouldn't miss in mind.
[SEG0045] person_4 (PATIENT): Well, uh, should I be worried about this?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I understand the worry. At the moment I'd say it's haemorrhoids, and we'll know more once the a colonoscopy is back.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think a colonoscopy makes sense here, for rectal bleeding. That will help us see what's going on underneath and decide the next step.
[SEG0048] person_4 (PATIENT): Okay, that's fine.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm sending you for blood tests because of rectal bleeding. We'll begin with lactulose, 15 ml, at night, for two weeks. You take it by mouth. It's for constipation. [SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): One warning sign to remember: you pass a lot of blood or feel faint. In that case don't wait. We'll catch up in three weeks. Look after yourself.
[SEG0051] person_4 (PATIENT): Thanks, that was helpful.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): See you then.

[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): right on time. Sit, please. How can I help?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): doctor, thank you for seeing us
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes, that's no problem at all please sit
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's hot flushes, doctor. She didn't want to come, but I insisted.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): how long has this been going on?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): probably three weeks yeah
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse.
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, you know, so it's severe, honestly. It's worse with caffeine and warm rooms. Sorry, I know I'm rambling a bit. Hmm, I've had irregular periods too, for two days. Uh, you know, as for night sweats, I honestly can't say when that began. It might have been last month or the month before.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Would you call it mild or bad?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): It's moderate, honestly.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): let's get your blood pressure and the other basics
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Rest your hand here...
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: SpO2 97 percent on room air, pulse 84, temp 36.7 degrees, pressure 122 over 75.
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): is that normal?
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll come back to those numbers
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you're comfortable, I'll examine you now.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll go gently.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure and pulse are fine, and there are no breast lumps on examination.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, you can sit back down.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding after sex or breast lumps at all?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No bleeding after sex or breast lumps, none of it.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, have you had palpitations, by any chance?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): um, I haven't noticed any palpitations
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Actually, doctor, I did notice palpitations. She doesn't always say.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, um, so no, I don't think I did. Maybe a little, I'm not sure.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'll note both what you've said and what you've noticed. Let me check a few things. Any weight loss or chest pain?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Hmm, none, as far as I know.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is your chest okay generally?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Uh, no, my breathing's been fine.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who's at home with you?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): It's just me and my wife at home now.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): are you working or retired?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Retired. I stopped a few years back.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): any diagnoses you've been given before?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I've had high blood pressure for about a year now. I'd rather know what's going on than keep guessing. I have thin bones. I've had an underactive thyroid, yes.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so high blood pressure and thin bones are already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today. Do you have any allergies to medicines, food, anything at all?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I mean, years back I got hives from penicillin, so I stay away from it now.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): what medicines are you taking at the moment?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): It's ramipril, 5 milligrams, maybe, every morning.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you got the box or the prescription on you?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so not with me. I'll bring it next time. Alendronate, once a week for my bones.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what strength is that?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): It's 70 milligrams. Thyronorm, 50 micrograms, every morning for my thyroid.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): So where does that leave us? The most likely explanation is perimenopausal symptoms. Anaemia is still possible.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): What are the chances it's something bad?
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): I can't promise yet, but most people with perimenopausal symptoms do well once it's treated properly. Stop me if I've got anything wrong. You've had hot flushes for three weeks, severe, and no breast lumps
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): That's it, yes.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): A bone density scan is what I'd like next, for menopause. I'm gonna order blood tests, for irregular periods. Layers of clothing, a fan by the bed, and cutting down on caffeine and spicy food can help the flushes. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose. Come back or go to emergency straight away if the symptoms get worse.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay, we're done for today take care
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): I think that's clear. Thank you for being so so thorough.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bye for now.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor, the receptionist said you'd see me now.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, do sit. Tell me what's been happening.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): So the thing is, I've got tingling in my fingers.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it begin?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): It's been five days now.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about an ache in the wrist, have you noticed that?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, about the same, six months. With ache in the wrist, I'd say moderate. It's a couple of times a week. Oh, and numbness in the thumb and first two fingers.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it happen all the time or in spells?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Honestly, once or twice a day. I've been waking up at night with pins and needles too, you know, since Monday.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's go through your medication. What are you taking?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm on thyroxine, every morning.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what strength is that?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): It's 75 micrograms.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when have you been taking it?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): For two months. Metformin, twice a day.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much do you take?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): 500 milligrams, I think that's what's on the box. Atorvastatin. I take it 20 milligrams, at night. I do miss it now and then, to be fair. I'd been on rosuvastatin, not any more though, I stopped.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you get any exercise?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I walk for about half an hour most days.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's your diet like?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I eat out quite a lot, to be honest.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before I prescribe anything, any allergies?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Right, I think I reacted to some antibiotic once, years ago. I don't remember which one, or what happened exactly.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any relatives with health problems I should be aware of?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): My uncle had colon cancer. Okay, you know, so my mother has migraines.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any surgery in your history?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I had my appendix out about eight years ago.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your general health, any conditions you're being treated for? I ask because it helps me narrow things down.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I have an underactive thyroid, for about ten years.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got diabetes.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything more?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got high cholesterol.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood. Alright, diabetes and high cholesterol, that matches what I have here. Any headache or weakness in the legs at all?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): No headache or weakness in the legs, none of it.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had any neck pain, trouble walking or bladder problems?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): No neck pain, trouble walking or bladder problems, none of it.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in the joints?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No swelling in the joints.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): How about your heart, any problems like that?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing like that.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any breathing difficulties apart from this?
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so no problems with breathing.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me measure a few things.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Rest your hand here...
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: temperature 36.7, BP is 123 over 70. And heart rate 64, SpO2 97 percent on room air.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's do the physical part now.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take your time, no rush.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bending the wrist for a minute brings on the numbness.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at this properly.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tapping over the wrist reproduces the tingling.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's all I need, thank you. Right, here's what I'm thinking. The most likely explanation is carpal tunnel syndrome. I can't rule out a pinched nerve in the neck yet. I think a blood sugar test makes sense here, for neuropathy screen. I'd like to arrange a nerve conduction study for hand numbness. Take short breaks from typing and keep the wrist straight. Do get help quickly if the symptoms get worse.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): See me again after the results are back.
[SEG0055] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright, I'll put it in my diary.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, I think we're finished. Is everything clear?
[SEG0057] person_1 (PATIENT): One thing: no, actually that's all. Thanks.
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): See you then.

[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had pain in your right ear before, or is this the first time?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): I had a similar thing a couple of years ago. It went away.

[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): I have asthma. High cholesterol, for about a year.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, any more?
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so high cholesterol is already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today. Do you have any known allergies at all?

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, almost done with this part.

[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Got it, thank you.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Call the clinic if you need us.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Thanks, that was helpful.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take care.

[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you for your time.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Safe journey home.

[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): About a six out of ten. Right, as for excess hair on my face, I honestly can't say when that began. It might have been last month or the month before. And acne along the jaw, too.

[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I gave up drinking about three years ago. I stay with my daughter and her family. I'm mostly vegetarian.

[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Dust. I come out in... well, itchy eyes.

[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): I had a C-section about ten years ago.

[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, and what else?
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, COPD is known to us, good to have that clear.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines do you take regularly?

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Thyronorm, 50 micrograms, every morning for my thyroid. Before this I was on glimepiride; that's been stopped.

[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none of that at all.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is your digestion otherwise okay?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that side's been fine.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's get your blood pressure and the other basics.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, give me a moment...
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: pressure 112 over 79, respiratory rate 14, temperature 36.5, heart rate 86.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that okay?
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, that's fine, we'll come to it.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, let me check a few things physically.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stay still while I have a look.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Facial acne along the jaw and some dark coarse hair on the chin.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, you can sit up. From what you've told me and what I found, I think we're dealing with possible polycystic ovary syndrome at this stage. A thyroid problem is still possible.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it something serious, doctor?
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's reasonable to be concerned, but right now possible polycystic ovary syndrome is my leading thought, not anything worse. Let's book hormone blood tests to look into irregular periods.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): We have a slot Tuesday at 2 pm, if that works.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order a thyroid test, for irregular periods. Regular exercise and modest weight loss can bring cycles back. Please come and see me after the results are back. Look after yourself.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mind how you go.

[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you describe it a bit more for me? How strong it is, what the pattern is, what helps.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): About a seven out of ten. Only holding on to things, and it's not much.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, have you noticed anything else alongside it?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): It usually comes with a blocked feeling in my ear.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has there been a recent cold too?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, I have.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your medical history?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): I have high blood pressure.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes.
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got diabetes.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, high blood pressure and diabetes are known to us, good to have that clear. Can you list what you take, tablets, creams or inhalers?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm on telmisartan, 40 milligrams, once a day. Sitagliptin. I take it 100 milligrams, maybe, once a day.

[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No, it's at home.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about your eating.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): I drink a lot of tea and snack through the day.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your job?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): I work in accounts at a hospital.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, before we go further, any allergies?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Not to my knowledge, no.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hold on, doctor, I think he reacted to naproxen once. I'm not certain, though.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't remember that.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, I'll write down both versions. Any surgery in the past?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): I, I had a meniscus repair on my knee four years ago.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had any ringing in the ears, slurred speech, headache or weakness?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no ringing in the ears, slurred speech, headache or weakness.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything on the skin I should know about?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Skin's normal.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is your digestion otherwise okay?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing unusual, no.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's start with the basic checks.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nearly finished here.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I can see a fine jerking of the eyes to the left and your walking is a little unsteady.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, that's enough for me.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Putting it all together, this looks most like an inner-ear balance problem such as vestibular neuritis. I'd also keep benign positional vertigo in mind. Let me repeat that back to make sure. You've had being unsteady, and no ringing in the ears or headache.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, that's right.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): I want blood tests done, that's for dizziness. I'm going to order a positional test, for vertigo. [SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): The thing that would worry me is if you get double vision, weakness or trouble speaking. If that happens, go to emergency. Please come and see me if it isn't settling in five days. That's all from me. Any questions?
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that's all. Thanks a lot.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): All the best.

[SEG0041] person_5 (PATIENT): It's a... um, I can't remember what it's called. It's a round yellow one.

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, what about your medical history? Just so I get the full picture.
[SEG0047] person_5 (PATIENT): I have high blood pressure, for about a year.

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so high blood pressure and migraines are already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today.
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): Here are the numbers, doctor. Heart rate 107, respiratory rate 19, temp 36.4 degrees. Blood pressure 95 over 56, oxygen saturation is 98 percent.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, let's have a proper look at you.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does that hurt?
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds are normal and the chest is clear.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel here.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your blood pressure drops when you stand, from the lying reading to standing.
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): All finished, thank you. Okay, thinking it through, this is probably postural low blood pressure, possibly related to medicines or dehydration. [SEG0062] person_5 (PATIENT): I think I understand everything. Thanks.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have a good day.

[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): None of those, no.

[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, I haven't had weight loss, black stools or difficulty swallowing, no.

[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No, uh, that's been fine.

[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Skin's normal.

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Grass pollen, I'd say.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you list what you take, tablets, creams or inhalers?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm on diclofenac, 50 milligrams, when needed. Antacid, when needed. I'd rather know what's going on than keep guessing.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): A few questions about your lifestyle now.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I live with my elderly mother. Yes, I work in a bakery, early starts. Lots of rice, lentils and some fruit.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think we're done unless you have questions.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): That's clear, thanks.

[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem at all, come in. What's troubling you?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Mainly burning pain in the upper tummy. There's a couple of other things, but that's the main one.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you take on a normal day? I'm asking so that we don't miss anything.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm on naproxen, twice a day.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): do you know the dose?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): It's 250 milligrams. Pantoprazole. I take it it 40 milligrams, before breakfast for my acidity.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did it come on recently?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): I'd say about four days. Actually, no, closer to to two days.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): alright, tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse these questions might sound routine, but they matter
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): yes, spicy food and empty stomach. That makes it worse. I get some relief from milk. And I've been feeling full quickly as well, for two weeks. About feeling full quickly, it's severe, honestly
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you notice any weight loss?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No weight loss, thankfully.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): any difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or jaundice?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I haven't had difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or jaundice, no.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): I follow. Have you noticed any weakness, or anything odd with your balance?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing odd there.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about your routine, work, habits, that sort of thing.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Not much, I mostly stay in these days. I drink a lot of tea and snack through the day. No, I share a house with my brother
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What conditions have you been treated for in the past?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I have arthritis in my knees sorry, I know I'm rambling a bit i've got acid reflux
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): right, right. Yes, arthritis in your knees is known to us, good to have that clear
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, are there any allergies I should be aware of?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): No allergies at all.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, has anyone in your family had anything serious?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): My grandfather had a stroke.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had any surgical procedures?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): yes, I had a bunion operation, six years ago
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at the area, I'll be gentle.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll listen to your chest now.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is soft with some tenderness in the upper middle part.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay, you can sit up now
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, thinking it through, my working impression is dyspepsia possibly related to anti-inflammatory tablets.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Will it clear up?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I understand the worry. At the moment I'd say it's dyspepsia possibly related to anti-inflammatory tablets, and we'll know more once the a test for the stomach germ is back.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): let's get a test for the stomach germ, for dyspepsia. Please stop taking the anti-inflammatory tablets for now and use paracetamol for the pain. Let's review you in four weeks. Anything else on your mind before you go?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Uh, okay, that makes sense. Thanks for explaining.

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come in, come in. Awful weather again, isn't it? Did you find somewhere to park, or did you do the usual lap round the block?
[SEG0002] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Third lap, and then I gave up and used the supermarket car park. It's a good job Mum has the wheelchair folded in the boot.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I told you to drop me at the door, Pauline. I'd have managed the ramp.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mrs Whitcombe, good to see you. Your daughter's right to be careful. Now, I understand the care home has been worried about your chest.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I've made some notes, doctor. I wrote them in the book the nurse gave me, so I'd not forget anything.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, please go ahead. Take your time, we're in no hurry.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): The cough began on Tuesday, so that's four days now. It was dry at first, and then I started bringing up yellowy-green phlegm, mostly first thing.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Four days, with the phlegm yellowy-green. Does the cough keep you awake?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): A little. I wake at about three and have to sit up.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What worries me is her breathing. She's breathless just walking to the lounge, and that's new. She used to do the whole corridor.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Pauline. Mrs Whitcombe, would you agree you're more breathless than usual?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): I'd say so. But I don't want a fuss.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): No fuss, just an honest picture. Have you had a temperature, any shivers?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no fever. The nurse took it on Wednesday and it was normal.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. And any pain in the chest when you cough or breathe in?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No chest pain. The ribs are sore from coughing, but nothing sharp.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): All right, that's useful. What about your tummy and appetite, any trouble with eating, or your bowels?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): All fine there. I'm eating my toast.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She is, but I'd say half portions, rather than full.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. Let me check your tablets. Do you have the list from the home?
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, here. Ramipril 5 mg once a day, and metformin 500 mg twice a day, and the water tablet in the morning, I don't have the name written.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, ramipril, metformin and a water tablet. Mrs Whitcombe, do you take the metformin twice a day?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Twice a day, every day. Breakfast and tea. I'm very regular about it.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mum, the night carer told me you push the evening one away quite often. She said it half the week.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): That's nonsense. I might have declined it once.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to referee. I'll note what both of you have told me, and the home can check their medicines chart.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now, any conditions of long standing? Things you'd have had for years?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Type 2 diabetes, hence the metformin. High blood pressure. And arthritis in the hands, which is why my handwriting is so poor.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your handwriting is perfectly clear, I can see the notebook. Now a question I always ask, any allergies?
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's one I'm not sure about. Years ago she came out in something after an antibiotic, but nobody can remember which one, or what it did. It might have been an allergy, it might not.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't remember it at all. I've never been told I was allergic to anything.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): So possibly allergic to an antibiotic, but no name and no clear reaction. I'll record it as uncertain, and we'll try to trace the old records.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can ask my brother, he kept all the paperwork when Dad died.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): That would help. Now I'll listen to your chest, if you're comfortable. Pauline, would you help your mum with her cardigan?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm perfectly capable of undoing a button.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Deep breaths in and out for me, through the mouth.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it a nasty one?
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): I want to see a picture before I say anything definite. I'd like to send you for a chest X-ray today, at the hospital over the road.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Today? We can do that. Does she need to be fasting?
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, nothing special. Just the usual ID, and wear something without metal on the chest.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): My buttons are plastic.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Perfect. In the meantime, plenty of fluids, sit up in the armchair rather than lying flat, and let the carers know if the breathing gets harder.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll tell the manager. She's on the ball.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Will I be able to go to the bingo on Thursday?
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's see how you feel on Thursday. Wrap up warm either way.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): I always do. I knitted this scarf myself.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's gorgeous. The X-ray department will give you the result to us, and the surgery will call the care home.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you for taking your time, doctor. She's been quite anxious.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not at all. She's been very clear, and I'd rather see people early. Mind the ramp on the way out.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. Good morning, doctor.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning to you both.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Come on, Mum, let's find that car before the supermarket charges us.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry we're late. The bus took forever, and then I forgot my backpack at the bus stop, so we had to go back.
[SEG0002] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's my fault, Doctor, I was still looking for the insurance card.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not a problem at all, you're here now. Hi there, buddy. So this is your asthma check-up. Tell me how you've been breathing lately.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, okay, I guess. Sometimes my chest feels kinda squeezy when I run around at recess.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Squeezy, I like that description. Is it like someone's hugging your chest too tight?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah, like that. And then I have to stop and sit down for a while.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's helpful. How long does the squeezy feeling last when you sit down?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Not long. Like, a few minutes? Then it goes away.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. And what about at night? Do you ever cough when you're in bed?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Sometimes I cough at night and it wakes me up. Only a little, though.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's more than a little, honey. I hear him coughing through the wall at least three nights a week, and some nights it goes on for a long time.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has the night cough been happening?
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): About one month, since the weather turned cold.
[SEG0014] person_4 (UNKNOWN): [from the hallway] He was wheezing a lot at the game on Saturday!
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I didn't catch who that was. But that's a good point to follow up on. Buddy, do you remember a whistling sound when you breathed at the game?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Kind of. Like a whistly sound when I breathe out. Not all the time.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Now, has he had any fever recently, or been sick with a cold?
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No fever. He had a little sniffle a couple of weeks ago, but nothing since then.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): And when he coughs, does he bring up any yellow or green phlegm?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing comes up. It's just a dry cough.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Let's talk about his medicines. Can you tell me what he takes and how?
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sure. There's the fluticasone, that's the daily inhaler. He's supposed to take it twice a day, morning and night, with the spacer.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I take it every day. I never forget.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Buddy, I'm sorry, but he skips the morning one a lot. We're always rushing for the bus. Nights I make sure of.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): I appreciate you both being honest. We'll come back to that. What else is he using?
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The albuterol, for when he gets wheezy. He takes it when he needs it, and I'd say maybe twice a week. And the montelukast, 5 mg chewable, at bedtime.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any other health problems, besides the asthma? I see eczema in his chart.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yeah, he still gets dry patches in the elbow creases.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. And any surgeries in the past?
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His mom told me he had his tonsils out when he was five.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good to know. Does anyone in the family have asthma, that you know of?
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His dad has asthma too.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): That fits the pattern, asthma often runs in families. Buddy, what do you like to do for fun, besides recess?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): I play soccer on Saturdays. I'm a goalie, so I don't run that much.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me get his numbers now. Sit tight, buddy.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 36.9 degrees Celsius, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, and breathing rate is 20 breaths per minute.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Oxygen saturation is 98 percent, and he weighs 72 pounds today.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Is that good, Doctor?
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): The numbers are all in a comfortable range, so nothing to worry about there. Now, how about his tummy and bowels, any problems there?
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, his stomach is fine.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Great. Let me explain what I think is going on. With the squeezy chest on running, the night cough several nights a week, and the wheeze at the game, it sounds like his asthma isn't fully controlled right now.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Is that because he misses the morning inhaler?
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Very likely. The daily inhaler calms the lining of the airways, but only if it's used every day, like brushing teeth.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): So I have to do it every morning?
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, and here's a trick: keep the inhaler right next to your toothbrush, and take your puffs before you brush. Then rinse your mouth.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That I can do. I'll put it right next to the toothbrush tonight.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wonderful. And the albuterol, buddy: take it before soccer, every Saturday.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not changing his medicines today, since I'd like to see first how he does when the daily inhaler is taken properly.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's see him again in six weeks, and we'll check how the cough and the squeezy chest are doing.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll book it at the front desk. And if he gets bad before then?
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he needs the albuterol more than usual, or he's struggling to breathe, call us right away or go to the emergency room.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thank you so much, Doctor. Come on, let's get you a snack.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, I've got numbness in my right hand and it's really scaring me. I keep thinking it's a stroke, or my spine.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Righto, let's sort it out. Which fingers are numb?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): The thumb, the pointer finger and the middle one. Not the little finger. And it's worse when I'm gripping something, like the steering wheel.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has it been going on?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): About two months.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it do anything else, besides numbness?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Tingling at night, like pins and needles. It wakes me up and I have to shake my hand out. And I've been dropping things, my coffee mug, a screwdriver last week.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): A sore ache in the wrist, and sometimes it runs up the forearm. Shaking it out helps a bit.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any pain in your neck?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no neck pain.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fall or injury to the wrist?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in the wrist or hand?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, not that I've noticed.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss lately?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my weight's been steady. If anything it's gone up.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I work on a production line, packing parts, same movement all day with a scanner gun.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll come to that. What medicines are you on?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Metformin, 500 mg twice a day, for the diabetes. Every day, never miss. Well, mostly. The evening one I sometimes forget.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. Anything else?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): There's a small white tablet for my cholesterol, I take it at night. I can't remember the name of it, my wife keeps the box.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Do you have any allergies?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Penicillin. I was told as a kid I'm allergic to it, but I honestly don't remember what happened.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine, I'll note it down. What other conditions have you got?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Type 2 diabetes, about six years. High cholesterol. Gout, though I haven't had a flare this year. And sleep apnoea, I use a machine at night.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Any operations?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): A hernia repair, about eight years ago.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family history of anything important?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had a heart attack at sixty. And my sister has carpal tunnel syndrome, she's a hairdresser.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Interesting. Do you smoke or drink?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I quit smoking five years ago. And I have two beers on the weekend, no more.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you exercise at all?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): I walk the dog on Sundays. That's about it, to be honest.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any chest pain or palpitations?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my heart feels fine.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): And passing urine, any trouble there, more than usual?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that's normal. I'm drinking the same as always.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check your numbers. Blood pressure is 136 over 84, pulse is 80 beats per minute.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hands out, palms up. I'll tap over the wrist crease here. Tell me what you feel.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Ow, tingling shoots into my fingers. That's exactly the feeling.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): The tapping over the wrist brings on the tingling. Now push the backs of your hands together, wrists bent, and hold for a minute.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): It's coming on already. Pins and needles in the same three fingers.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yep. Bending the wrist like that brings on the same tingling. Now light touch on each fingertip, eyes closed.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): It's duller on the thumb and the first two fingers. The little finger feels normal.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Reduced feeling in the thumb, index and middle fingers, then. And squeeze my fingers as hard as you can.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Like this? It doesn't feel strong.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grip is a little weaker on the right than the left. Based on all this, it looks like carpal tunnel syndrome, where a nerve gets squeezed in the wrist.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): So it's not a stroke? Or my spine?
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nothing here points to either. Your job could well be the trigger.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): What do we do about it?
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to arrange a nerve conduction study, to measure how well the nerve is working. And a blood test for your HbA1c, to check your sugar control.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. And if the nerve test is normal?
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then I might consider an X-ray of your neck, but we'll hold off on that for now.
[SEG0056] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor, I've got a wrist splint in the right size here. Shall I show him how to put it on?
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please do. Wear it at night, so the wrist stays straight while you sleep. And take short breaks from the scanner gun during the day.
[SEG0058] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll do it, and I'll tell my supervisor. And the follow-up?
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if it's not better in four weeks, and bring the tablet box this time so we can get its name.
[SEG0060] person_1 (PATIENT): Right, my wife will find it. Thank you, doctor.

- Use only what is said. Never invent or infer. Leave out every field and section that has no information.
- Record who said it (doctor, patient, nurse, caregiver, family_member, clinical_staff, unknown), in lower case.
- A denied finding goes in negative_findings, never in symptoms. A doctor's question is not a fact: use the answer.

Transcript (encounter 00568)
[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning. Mr Gopal Rathore, correct? And you are...?
[SEG0002] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Good morning, doctor. I am Sunita, I stay with him as his carer. Yes, he is Mr Rathore.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, yes, Gopal Rathore. You know, the lift downstairs was not working, so we took the stairs very slowly, and that itself shows the problem.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let us start there, then. What is the problem?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I am more breathless than last winter, doctor. Last winter also I was breathless, but this time it is more, and my grandson's wedding is in March, so I told Sunita...
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): One thing at a time, please. How long has this extra breathlessness been going on?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks, I think. Only two weeks.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three weeks, sir. I am counting from the day you stopped walking to the park.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two, three weeks. So roughly two to three weeks, let us say. Any cough with it?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, cough also, every morning, with some white phlegm. That one is old, it is always there.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): White phlegm, fine. Any wheezing, any whistling sound in the chest?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Wheezing, yes, at night, when I lie down. I hear it myself, and Sunita also hears.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No chest pain, doctor. That I would have told you immediately.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Coughing up any blood?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No blood, no. Only the white phlegm.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Any swelling in your legs or ankles?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling in my legs, doctor. These legs are the same as always.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sir, his ankles are swollen in the evenings, doctor. When I take off his socks they leave deep marks.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. We will come back to that. Now medicines. Which inhalers and tablets are you on?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Tiotropium inhaler, once a day in the morning. And the blue inhaler, salbutamol, when I am breathless, which is many times now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And tablets?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): One small white tablet for the pressure. The name I cannot recall, my daughter wrote it somewhere. Sunita, what is it?
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I am sorry, doctor, only the box has the name and it is at home. White, small, round, once in the morning.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any other health problems?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): COPD, ten years now. Also high blood pressure, and diabetes, controlled by diet only. Arthritis in the knees also, that is why I do not walk much.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations in the past?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Cataract operation, five years ago, left eye. And my appendix, in 1988.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, penicillin. I get a rash all over. A doctor in 1990 told me never to take it.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. In the family, any chest or heart problems?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): My father died of a heart attack at sixty. My brother has asthma, he lives in Pune, a funny man, once he...
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Did you ever smoke?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, thirty years I smoked, beedis. I stopped eight years back.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I do not drink alcohol at all. I was a bank clerk, retired now, and bank people are careful, you know.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let me check your vitals, then listen to your chest.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, of course. Sunita, hold my shawl.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure 138 over 82, pulse 96, oxygen 91 percent, breathing rate 22, temperature 37.2 degrees.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Is the oxygen low? My neighbour had oxygen once...
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): A little low for a normal person, but you have COPD. Now deep breaths in and out, mouth open.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Like this? Cough, sorry.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): There is wheeze on both sides, and the air entry is reduced at the bottom of both lungs. Your lips are not blue, which is good.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Quickly, how are your stomach and bowels? And passing urine?
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Stomach is fine, fine. Urine also normal.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): So this looks like a COPD flare-up, probably an infection on top of the old problem. But I cannot rule out fluid on the lungs yet.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Fluid? In my lungs? My uncle also had fluid and...
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please, Mr Rathore, listen. I will order a chest X-ray and blood tests today, and a lung function test, spirometry.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): All today? Sunita has to cook lunch at one o'clock.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): X-ray and blood tests today. Spirometry I am booking for next week, reception will give you the date.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): And if the swelling in the ankles continues, I might arrange an echocardiogram, a heart scan, to look at the heart.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): Heart scan? My heart is strong, doctor.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Continue both inhalers as you are, and use the blue one when needed. I want to see you again if you are not better in one week.
[SEG0054] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And if he is worse in the night, doctor? Should I call you?
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he cannot speak full sentences, or his lips turn blue, call an ambulance straight away.
[SEG0056] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, can I bathe in cold water? My grandson says it is good for health.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Warm water is fine, Mr Rathore. Avoid very cold air and keep the windows shut at night.
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will make sure, doctor. Thank you.
[SEG0059] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. And please come to the wedding also, there will be good food.
[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ha, we shall see. Take care, both of you.

[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, a couple of weeks ago, I guess. But it's been on and off for about two months, if you count the earlier ones.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): So two months of it coming and going, with this stretch being the latest. What does it feel like?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Kind of scratchy, like I swallowed a handful of gravel. Worse when I first wake up.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Gravel, got it. Anything else going on, besides the throat?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): There's these lumps under my jaw. They feel like little peas, right here, on both sides.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Those are lymph glands. Think of them as the guard posts on the road into your head, they swell up when there's trouble in the neighborhood.
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Huh. That makes sense, actually.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had a fever with this?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah, last week I had one, I was kind of shivery for a couple days. But that went away on Sunday.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Fever gone, then. Any cough with it?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, not really. Just the throat.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And is swallowing hard, like food getting stuck?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, it hurts a little, but nothing gets stuck.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let's talk about what you're taking. What's in your medicine cabinet right now?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): There's my blood pressure pill, lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day. I take it with my coffee.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Great. Anything else, even stuff from the drugstore?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Tylenol, 500 mg, when it's bad. Probably most days, honestly. And those throat lozenges, I get through a few a day.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. That's three things, then. Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Nope, no allergies that I know of. I've taken everything.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Now, I'll read your numbers. Hold still for a second.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 37.1 °C, and pulse is 76. Both nice and calm.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swab result in a day or two, bloods a bit longer. The front desk will call you.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then take as many quiet minutes as you can steal. Even small breaks help.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. I'll sneak some in at lunch.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in one week, to go through the results together.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): One week. Okay, I'll book it at the desk.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. And keep the Tylenol at the dose you're using, don't push past it.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): Right, I won't.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else bugging you today?
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Just the parking validation, I forgot to bring the ticket. Never mind.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): The front desk can stamp it for you on the way out.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): Sounds good. Thanks, doc.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're welcome. Go see the nurse for the swab on your way out.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): Will do. Bye.

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hi, come on in. Wow, you look soaked. Is it still pouring out there?
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Pouring. And the parking garage was full, so I walked six blocks. I'm sorry, I'm a few minutes late.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not at all. Sit, catch your breath. We have plenty of time today.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you. I made notes, if that's okay. I didn't want to forget anything.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please, notes are a gift. What would you like to start with?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): I found a lump in my left breast, in the shower last week. I wrote down the date, and the time.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): That must have been frightening. Tell me what you noticed.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): It's about the size of a pea, firm, on the outer side. And it's a little tender when I press it.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. And how long do you think it has been there?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): That's the thing, I really can't say. It might have been last month, or the month before. I only noticed it last week.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's very common. These lumps are usually found by accident. Have you seen any fluid from the nipple?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): And any change in the skin, like dimpling or puckering?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No dimpling. I checked in the mirror, twice.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Now, tell me about your health in general. Anything ongoing?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): An underactive thyroid. That's the only thing.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what do you take for it?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Levothyroxine. I think it's maybe 75 micrograms? I'd have to check the box.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's fine, we can confirm it with your pharmacy. Once a day, in the morning?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Every morning, before breakfast. I'm quite strict about that one.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wonderful. Anything else you take regularly?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): The contraceptive pill, once a day, in the evening. Although, I have to be honest, I miss it some evenings.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you for telling me. Is it most evenings you remember, or fewer?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): I take it every day, I believe. But my diary has a few gaps, so I'm not certain.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Then let's say we're not certain, and we'll come back to it.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that important for the lump?
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): It can be, hormones play a role in how breast tissue behaves, which is why I ask.
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): I see. I wrote that my aunt had breast cancer. I should have said that first.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you did. Which side of the family is your aunt on?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother's side. She was diagnosed in her fifties.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Knowing that, we'll be a little more careful with you.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): So what do you think this is? Please be honest.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Honestly, from your description, a small, firm, tender lump, it's most likely a benign cyst. But I won't leave it at a guess.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): What do we do, then?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll order a breast ultrasound, so we can see exactly what it is. The scheduler will call you with an appointment.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): And if it's something worse?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we'd know early, and we'd act. Right now, there's nothing to suggest that, so please try not to spiral.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll try. I keep imagining things.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): I understand. I'd like to see you again next Friday, to go over the ultrasound together.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Next Friday. I'll put it in my notes. Thank you for taking time, doctor.

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning. Ms Anjali Deshmukh, is that correct?
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Good morning.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please sit. I have a note from reception about your breasts. Tell me what is happening.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing much, actually. Just breast tenderness before my periods. I thought I should mention it.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when are you having this tenderness?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): About six months now. It is not a big problem.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it come at a particular time of the month?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, the week before my period. Then it goes away once the period starts.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): That pattern is useful to know. Is anything else also happening in that week?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): A little bloating. My stomach feels tight. I am also irritable, my husband says.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): I see. And what about headaches?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Headaches, yes. But I cannot tell you when they began. Maybe a year, maybe longer. I never wrote it down.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): That is fine, we will not worry about the exact timing. Any nipple discharge?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No discharge.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any lump that you have felt in either breast?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No lumps. I checked in the bath.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Any fever recently?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now, your medicines. What are you taking regularly?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Metformin, 500 mg, twice a day.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Every day, twice?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, twice a day. Though some nights I forget the second one. So I am not sure I take it every single day.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you for being honest. That is important for us. What else?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Levothyroxine, in the morning. I think 50 micrograms, maybe? I am not fully sure.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will confirm the dose from your records. Anything else?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): A vitamin D capsule, 60000 units, once a week on Sundays.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Do you have any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, sulpha drugs. My mother told me. I do not remember what reaction happened.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Sulpha drugs, reaction not remembered. I will note it clearly.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medical conditions do you have, along with those tablets?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): PCOS, since college. Thyroid problem, hypothyroidism. And sugar, type 2 diabetes.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): PCOS, hypothyroidism and type 2 diabetes. Have you had any operations?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Appendix removal, in 2015.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any illnesses in your family that I should know about?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): My father has high blood pressure. That is all.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what work do you do?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): I am a software engineer. Sitting job, mostly.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you drink alcohol?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I do not drink alcohol.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your diet?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Vegetarian, always.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Now, let me take some measurements.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure 124 over 80. Pulse 76. Oxygen saturation 99 percent.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it normal?
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Quite normal. Your weight is 62 kilos and your height is 160 centimetres. That gives a BMI of 24.2.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): How is your breathing generally? Any trouble?
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Breathing is fine.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your heart, any chest pain or racing?
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Heart is fine also.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Now I will examine your breasts. Please lie back.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Both breasts look symmetrical. There is mild tenderness on pressing, on both sides.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, that is the tender place.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am now checking under the arms. The glands there are not enlarged.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): That is good, no?
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, good. You can sit up now. Let me explain my thinking step by step.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain before periods is usually related to hormone changes. I cannot rule out fibrocystic breast changes, which are harmless but common.
[SEG0057] person_1 (PATIENT): Fibrocystic? Is it cancer?
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, it is not a cancer. I only mention the name so you know what we are considering.
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): I also cannot rule out a thyroid or hormone imbalance contributing, since you have the thyroid condition.
[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): So I would like to order a thyroid function test, and a prolactin level.
[SEG0061] person_1 (PATIENT): Blood test?
[SEG0062] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, one sample. I will add an HbA1c as well, to check your sugar control.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will also arrange a breast ultrasound, just to be thorough.
[SEG0064] person_1 (PATIENT): When can I do it?
[SEG0065] person_2 (DOCTOR): The front desk will give you a slot. Please do all tests this week.
[SEG0066] person_1 (PATIENT): I will go today.
[SEG0067] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. For the tenderness, a well-fitting supportive bra helps, and cutting down caffeine.
[SEG0068] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please come back in three weeks with the reports, and we will decide the next step together.
[SEG0069] person_1 (PATIENT): Three weeks, I will book it. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0070] person_2 (DOCTOR): You are welcome. Take care of yourself, and do not downplay things next time.

[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you, doctor. ~
