[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, it's the shoulder. I can't lift my arm above my head any more, I was trying to reach the press and, ah, I just couldn't.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which side, and how long?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): The right. Three weeks now, give or take.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it hurt or is it just stuck?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Both, sure. There's a sort of, an ache at night, mostly, when I lie on it.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything when you move it?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): There's a clicking. Started... I'm not sure when. Before the weakness, I think? Or maybe along with it. I couldn't tell you.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Any fall or knock to it?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no fall. I didn't hurt it.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Neck pain?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Not really, no. The neck's grand.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or pins and needles down the arm?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever or feeling unwell with it?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I'm well in myself.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medicines. What are you on?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Ramipril for the pressure, 5 mg, once a day. Atorvastatin, 20 mg, at night. And paracetamol, 1 gram, up to four times a day, for the shoulder.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Are you allergic to anything, any allergies?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah. Maybe. I think I came out in a rash, years ago, after one of the antibiotics. But I couldn't tell you which one.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record that as unconfirmed. Health history, apart from the shoulder?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure, high cholesterol, the gout, and the arthritis in my knees.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): A knee replacement, the left one, about six years ago.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heart or joint problems in the family?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had a heart attack at sixty. And my sister has rheumatoid arthritis.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I gave up smoking in 2015.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): A glass of wine at the weekend, I'd say. Sure, that's all.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at it. Pulse 74, blood pressure 142 over 86, temperature 36.5, oxygen 97 percent, breathing 16, weight 91 kilos.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Is the pressure all right? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): A touch up from the pain, I'd say. Now lift your arm out to the side for me.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): That's as high as it goes. ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, I can see you can only lift the arm to shoulder height. And there's tenderness at the front of the right shoulder.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, that's sore. ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with your chest, breathlessness on exertion?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that, my chest is fine.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. This looks most like a rotator cuff problem, the tendons that lift the arm.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it a tear? ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Could be partial, which is why I'd like to arrange an X-ray of the shoulder and an ultrasound scan of the shoulder.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Grand. Will that be today? ~
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): The ultrasound is booked by reception. I'd also like to do a blood test for inflammation.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine so. What about the pain at night? ~
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep taking the paracetamol, and try a pillow under the arm when you lie down.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll do that. ~
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in two weeks with the results.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks, so. Thanks, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I've been keeping a note of this, so I can be precise. My heart pounds at night, and has done for about a month.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that's really useful. Tell me what it feels like.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): A thumping, in the chest and sometimes in my throat, quite fast. It wakes me up, usually between two and four.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long does an episode last?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Anywhere from a couple of minutes to, last Tuesday, I'd say twenty minutes.
[SEG0006] person_3 (UNKNOWN): [from the corridor] It was nearer half an hour, last Tuesday.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, someone's talking out there. Ignore that. It lasted a good while, anyway.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll go by what you tell me. Does anything come with it, dizziness, sweating?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Dizzy spells, yes. Occasionally I feel light-headed when I stand up in the morning. I can't say when that began.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Roughly, before the thumping, or after?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): I honestly don't know. I only noticed it recently.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. And do you sweat at night?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Sometimes, after the thumping. My pyjamas get damp.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No pain, none whatsoever.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you fainted, or come close to it?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No, never fainted.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about caffeine and alcohol? Tell me what you have in a typical day.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): About four cups of strong tea, usually the last at around eight in the evening. And I drink wine at the weekend, a glass or two.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to anything?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No allergies.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check your numbers. ~
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Please. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pulse 74 and regular, blood pressure 124 over 78, temperature 36.6, oxygen 99 percent, breathing 14 a minute, and you weigh 66 kilos.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): All normal? ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): All normal. Any cough or breathlessness at all?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my breathing is fine.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any ankle swelling or tiredness, anything with the heart?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling. Nothing like that.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me listen. Breathe normally.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it a murmur? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your heart sounds are normal, no murmurs, and your pulse is regular.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): That's a relief. So what's causing the thumping? ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weighing it all up, the most likely cause is the caffeine, especially the tea late into the evening. I'd say caffeine-related palpitations.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): I have been drinking more since I took on the extra project. ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): That would do it. Cut the tea down to two cups, none after noon, and see what happens over the next fortnight.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Two cups. That will be a trial. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): And alcohol late in the evening can trigger it too, so keep the wine to earlier in the day. ~
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll bear it in mind. And if it doesn't stop? ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep your diary going. If it gets worse, lasts more than half an hour, or you feel faint or get chest pain, come in straight away.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Understood. Thank you for being so reassuring. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late, doctor, traffic was dreadful. Marcia drove me. ~
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem. Mr Delaney, what brings you in? ~
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, it's nothing much. I've been feeling a bit low since Dorothy passed. My daughter thinks I should come.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry for your loss. How long ago?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): About three months. I'm managing, you know.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's not eating, doctor. He's lost weight, his trousers are held up with a belt now.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I eat fine. I just don't have much appetite.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mr Delaney, is that right, you don't have much appetite? ~
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit less, maybe. That's all.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are you sleeping?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Sleeping fine. No trouble sleeping.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dad, you're up at three every single night. I hear the kettle.
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): I get a cup of tea. It's not a problem. ~
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or of harming yourself?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He wouldn't say if he did, but he hasn't said anything like it to me. ~
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. What medicines do you take?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day. And metformin, 500 mg, twice a day.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's 20 mg, Dad. I fill the pill box. The lisinopril is 20.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm sure it's 10, it's what Dorothy used to give me.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll check the lisinopril dose with the pharmacy. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Well. In hospital once something gave me a rash, I think. I don't know what it was. Marcia may remember.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't. They never told us.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record it as a possible allergy. What other health conditions do you have?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure, diabetes, the type two, and arthritis in my hands.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): A hernia repair, back in 2008.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family with depression?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): My brother Frank had it, years ago.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are you living at the moment?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): On my own now, in the same house. I'm a widower.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): And before you retired?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I was a mechanic for forty years. Retired now.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check your numbers. Blood pressure 134 over 80, pulse 72, temperature 36.5, oxygen 97 percent, breathing 16, and your weight is 70 kilos.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's six kilos down from last year. ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. Let me look at you. You look a little thin, and your eyes are tired.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Everybody says I look tired. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's no swelling in your ankles. And your heart sounds are normal.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): That's good, isn't it? ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with your breathing or chest?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing. Breathing's fine.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your tummy, any vomiting or pain?
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing there either.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like a grief reaction to me, but I can't rule out depression, and I want to check your body too.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): There's nothing wrong with my body. ~
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Maybe not, but I'd like to arrange a thyroid blood test, a vitamin B12 level, an HbA1c, and kidney function.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): All today? ~
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Today, yes. And please eat small meals more often.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): If you say so. ~
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the sleep and appetite haven't improved in four weeks, come back and we'll talk about support and counselling.
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure he does. ~

[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Raghu is fine, everyone calls me that. I was a schoolteacher, you know, forty years, and they still call me Sir at the vegetable shop.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sir it is, then, in the vegetable shop. And this is? ~
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Sunita, I stay with him as his carer. I'm here because the evenings are very difficult now.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the evenings.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He gets confused. After the lights come on he asks me where his wife is, and she passed ten years ago. It started about three months ago, I'd say.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no, it's not three months. It began last month, one month, maybe, when the clocks changed.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): One month, or three months. We'll note somewhere between one and three months. And what happens during the confusion, Raghu?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): I get a bit muddled. It's the television, it confuses me. ~
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is he restless too, Sunita?
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes, in the evenings he paces. Up and down the corridor, it takes an hour to settle him.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any falls?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No falls. I am a very steady man.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sir, you fell in the bathroom two weeks ago. I helped you up.
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): That was a slip, it was nothing.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record that Sunita saw a fall and you say it didn't happen. Any fever or cold symptoms recently?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): None of that.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines is he taking, Sunita?
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day. Donepezil, 5 mg, at night. And tamsulosin, 400 micrograms, after dinner.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): And any allergies to medicines, Raghu?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I have no allergies. None.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sir, the antibiotic you had at the hospital last year, you were so itchy. I don't know which one it was.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't remember any itching.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll keep both. Health problems, Raghu?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure, and the prostate, it's enlarged.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Cataract, both eyes, two years ago. Very good surgeon.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who is at home with you?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I live in with him, his son visits at the weekends.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Raghu, can you tell me today's date? ~
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): It's... Tuesday? No, I'm not sure. Sunita will know. ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you know where we are?

[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Slowly, sir, take your stick. ~

[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): I told you, steady. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble passing water, Raghu?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing now, the tablet helps.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): What I think is happening is evening confusion, what we call sundowning, and I'd like to rule out other causes.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Is it serious, doctor? ~

[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): When should I bring him? ~

[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll do that. ~
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in two weeks, and Sunita, write down what happens each evening.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning, Mr Iyer. Terrible rain today. Did you manage to park? ~
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Yes, thank you, third floor of the car park, very inconvenient, but I managed. ~
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Always the third floor. So, the knee. Tell me from the beginning. ~
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Certainly. My right knee locks, sometimes it gets stuck and I cannot straighten it. This has been going on for two months.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Locks how, stuck bent?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, bent, about thirty degrees I think. Then I wiggle it and it clicks free.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Interesting. And does it also let you down?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, giving way. On the stairs mostly, going down. Last week I nearly fell at the office.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): After badminton on Sundays, it swells up like a small football.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): And pain on the stairs?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Pain, yes, on the inside of the knee when I climb the stairs.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you fall or twist it?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No fall, no twisting that I recall.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any redness or heat over the knee?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No redness, no heat.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever, doctor.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's go through your tablets.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Metformin, 500 mg, twice a day, every day, I take it regularly. Well, mostly. I sometimes miss the evening one if I come home late.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day. And diclofenac, maybe 50 mg? When the knee is bad. I will check the packet.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No allergies, none that I know of.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your other health conditions?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and some osteoarthritis in the other knee.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any previous operations?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): My appendix as a teenager, and a hernia repair in 2015.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Diabetes in the family?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother had diabetes.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I am a bank manager, so much sitting.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you drink?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't drink any alcohol.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): And badminton, how often?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Every Sunday morning with my son. I would hate to give it up.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, let me see the knee. Pulse 78, blood pressure 130 over 82, temperature 36.6, oxygen 98 percent, breathing 16, and weight 80 kilos.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): A little high, the pressure? ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): A touch, nothing alarming. Lie back, please. I'm going to bend the knee.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah, that is the sore spot. ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's tenderness along the inner joint line, and I can feel a click when I bend and rotate it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that the lock? ~
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Possibly. Any trouble with your breathing, chest, anything like that?
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): My impression is a torn meniscus, the cartilage in the knee, but the scan will tell.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Will I need surgery? ~
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Maybe not. I'd like to arrange an MRI of the knee, and an X-ray of the knee as well.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): And how soon? ~
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): The MRI is a few weeks. I'd also like to do a blood test for your HbA1c, since the sugar affects healing.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): And is badminton allowed? ~
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd rest it until the scan. Also, let's get a physiotherapist to see you.
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): Very well. ~
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it locks again before the scan, come back sooner and we'll see you urgently.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, understood, thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Is it infected? ~

[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. Yes. Hm. ~

[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That's what I said. ~

[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all.

Transcript (encounter 00766)
[SEG0001] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning, doctor. I'm Dad's daughter, Kate. He's here for his repeat prescription review, he says he feels well.
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): I do feel well. I don't see why we had to come. ~
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's good to hear, Mr Sutcliffe. It's a routine check, so don't worry. How's your breathing?
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. A bit puffed on the hill, that's all.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dad, you stop three times on the hill.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Kate, thanks for saying so. Any swelling in your ankles, Mr Sutcliffe?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): A little at night, maybe. It goes by morning.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dizziness, or fainting?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Waking at night short of breath?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I sleep like a baby.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you taking at the moment?
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Furosemide, 40 mg, once a day, in the morning. That's the water tablet.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Codeine, it makes me sick as a dog.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your conditions?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has heart failure, diagnosed two years ago, and high blood pressure.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any heart problems in the family?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): My father died of a heart attack at sixty.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And who looks after you at home?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I live with Kate and her husband now, since my wife died.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Pulse, pressure, and your weight. ~
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Go on. ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pulse 74, blood pressure 128 over 76, oxygen 96 percent, weight 82 kilos.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that more than last time? ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's up by two kilos from three months ago, which could be fluid. Let me look at your ankles and listen to your chest. ~
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's mild swelling above both ankles, and your chest has a few crackles at the bottom of both lungs.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that bad? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's mild, but it fits with a little fluid build-up, so I'd say your heart failure is stable but slightly fluid-overloaded.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I feel fine. ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Many people do, until it builds. I'd like to keep the same tablets for now, and ask you to weigh yourself every morning.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should I write it down? ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, same scales, same time, after the toilet. If your weight goes up by two kilos in three days, ring us.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll keep a chart. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cut down on salt, and don't add any at the table.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): My wife used to say that. ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): She was right. I'd like to see you again in four weeks, to check your weight and your ankles.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Four weeks. Fine. Thank you. ~
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Morning! It's my hands again. The arthritis. It flared up, since the cold weather started, and I'm back to square one.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry to hear that. Which joints, and how bad?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): The knuckles and the base of my thumbs, both hands. Stiff and sore, especially in the morning. I can't open jars.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long does the morning stiffness last?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): An hour, an hour and a half. It was ten minutes in the summer.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling or redness, or fever?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit of swelling in the knuckles. No redness. No fever.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain in other joints, like your knees, hips or spine?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my knees are okay. Just the hands.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any rash or dry eyes?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No rash. My eyes are fine.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking, and how did the treatment go after our last visit?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): A gel for the thumbs, I can't remember the name, I got it from the pharmacy. And naproxen, maybe 250 mg, twice a day, on and off.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the gel you can't name, and naproxen 250 mg twice a day as you recall it. Any other history?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Osteoarthritis diagnosed years ago, and I had a stomach ulcer once.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you have any allergies?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Years ago, a rash from penicillin, but I've avoided it ever since.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Let me look at your hands. Put them on the table, palms down. ~
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Here.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's bony swelling of the end joints and the base of both thumbs, and tenderness with a bit of warmth in two knuckles, no redness.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it getting worse? ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's an osteoarthritis flare, as you say, but with the long morning stiffness and warm knuckles, I can't rule out an inflammatory arthritis, such as rheumatoid, on top of it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Rheumatoid! Oh no. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's a possibility, not a diagnosis. The key difference is the length of the morning stiffness, which is over an hour for you. ~
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): What do we do? ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep using the gel, warm your hands in the morning, and wear thin gloves in cold weather.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I always forget gloves. ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Put a pair by the front door. And take the naproxen with food only.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the knuckle swelling gets worse, you get new swelling in other joints, or the stiffness lasts all morning, come back to see me and I'll arrange blood tests and a referral.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. Thanks, doctor. ~

[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): That's right. I've a wee gadget at home, and it said 88, on Monday, and I nearly dropped dead. ~
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning. Come in. Which number is low, and when?
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): 88 percent, then 90, 89. It was the same morning and evening, for three days.
[SEG0005] person_3 (NURSE): His oxygen today is 93 on our machine.
[SEG0006] person_4 (UNKNOWN): [from the corridor] It said 87 on Tuesday, I saw it!
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll go by what you tell me, Mr Brennan. How have you been feeling?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit breathless on the hill, and a cough. A dry one.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Since the cold, three weeks ago.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or sweats?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in your legs, or waking at night breathless?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking at the moment?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): A small white tablet for the water, I couldn't tell you the name, from the heart clinic. And a blood-thinner, 5 mg, maybe? Twice a day.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll check with the record, the white one and the dose of the blood-thinner. Any operations?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): A hernia repair, in 2010.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your family history?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): My father died of emphysema. He smoked like a chimney.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Aileen, can we do his observations on our machine, and walk him down the corridor with it on? ~
[SEG0024] person_3 (NURSE): Of course.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. His oxygen was fine at rest, and it dropped a little with walking, then came back up.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it dangerous? ~
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Those home devices can be inaccurate, especially with cold hands or nail varnish, but your breathlessness and cough deserve checking. ~
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd say this might be a lingering chest infection, and I'm going to start you on an antibiotic, doxycycline, 100 mg twice a day, for a week.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): And I'd like you to have an inhaler, salbutamol, two puffs when you're short of breath.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please come back in a week, and I'll check your chest again.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): A week. Thank you. ~
[SEG0035] person_3 (NURSE): I'll give you the leaflets. ~

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning. How would you like to be addressed, Mr Arkwright, or Walter? ~
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Mr Arkwright, if you'd be so kind. This is my son, Philip, who insisted on driving me. ~
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dad's been coughing up green sputum and I think it's a chest infection, so I booked it.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Philip. Mr Arkwright, when did the green sputum start?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Let me think. It was before the Bank Holiday. Or just after it. I really couldn't say with any confidence.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Early last month, Dad? Or was it after the anniversary? I can't pin it down either.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's all right. Do you wheeze?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, particularly at night. A sort of whistle when I breathe out.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): And how is your energy?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Poor. I'm tired all day.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you cough up blood?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Certainly not.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever or shivers?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No pain, no.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight loss?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): None that I'm aware of.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swollen ankles?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my ankles are as they've always been.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): What inhalers do you use?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Tiotropium, maybe 18 micrograms, once a day, though I'd have to check the box. And salbutamol, when I'm wheezy.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll verify the tiotropium. Any allergies?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Septrin. I broke out in a rash.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medical history?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): COPD, high blood pressure, osteoporosis, and reflux.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Operations?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): A hip replacement in 2019, and cataracts in 2021.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lung problems in the family?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had emphysema. My sister has asthma.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): You smoked, I think.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): I gave up smoking twelve years ago. Forty a day for forty years, before that.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): A sherry at Christmas.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who's at home?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I live with Philip now.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your work?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I was a factory foreman. Retired for eleven years.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Oxygen 92 percent, pulse 88, temperature 37.6, breathing 20, blood pressure 142 over 84, weight 70 kilos.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is the oxygen low? ~

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Perfect. I can hear crackles at the right base, and wheeze throughout both lungs.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that serious? ~
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's no swelling in the legs, which is good. Any trouble with your heart, palpitations, fluttering?
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your tummy, any trouble with your bowels?
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing, all regular.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like a chest infection on top of the COPD, but I can't rule out pneumonia.

[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does tremor run in the family? ~
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had it. We called it the family shake. ~

[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Does it need tablets? ~

[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Since... the summer? No. The summer before. Or maybe the spring. I honestly can't tell you, it just sort of arrived.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it ease off once you're up? ~
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): After about ten minutes, yes, then it comes back after I've been sitting. ~
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anywhere else in the foot?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Along the arch, a tight ache, yes.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Calves?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Very tight, yes. I get cramp after shifts.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or tingling in the foot?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No numbness.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you twist it or injure it?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I never injured it.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling, no.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for it?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Naproxen, maybe 250 mg? Twice a day. And omeprazole, 20 mg, once a day. Every morning. Well, most mornings. I forget it on my days off.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Tramadol. I react to it. I've been told. But don't ask me what it does to me.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Medical history?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Reflux, flat feet, and carpal tunnel in both wrists.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Surgery?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Bunion surgery in 2012. And a hysterectomy in 2019.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother has arthritis in her feet.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's your job?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Nurse, twelve-hour shifts on a surgical ward.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Exercise?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I run, parkrun on Saturdays. Or I did.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): And on shift?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Hard floors all day. About eight miles a shift, the app says.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Blood pressure 128 over 80, weight 82 kilos.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Same as last time? ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Same. Sit up on the couch. I'm pressing the heel.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Ow! There. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's tenderness at the inner side of the heel, and your calf muscles are very tight.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Told you. ~
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your arches are flat when you stand.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, always have been. ~
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with your breathing?
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing, I'm fine.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like plantar fasciitis, but I can't rule out a heel spur.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): What's the difference? ~
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): A spur is a bony lump you can see on X-ray. I'd like to arrange an X-ray of the foot, and an ultrasound of the heel.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it a long wait? ~
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): A few weeks. I'd also like to do blood tests for inflammation, and refer you to a podiatrist for insoles.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. And what do I do meanwhile? ~
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stretch the calves three times a day, and roll your foot over a frozen water bottle.
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll try, thank you. ~
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not better in six weeks, come back and we'll talk about an injection.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, six weeks. Sorry again about being late. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi. Sorry, it's probably nothing. Dan made me come.
[SEG0002] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's not nothing. She's been throwing up for days.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning to you both. Let's start with you, though. What's been happening?
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): I've just been a bit queasy. Since I found out I was pregnant, really. It's what everyone gets, isn't it?
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about the queasy feeling.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): It's pretty constant, I suppose, though worse in the mornings. It's only been about two weeks.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three weeks, Em. It started the weekend we went to your mum's. That's three weeks on Saturday.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it? I thought two weeks. Maybe it is three.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between two and three weeks. And the being sick, how often is that happening?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, three or four times a day. Sometimes more. It's not that bad, honestly.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): On Tuesday it was more like five. She was bringing up water by the end.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hm. What else have you noticed?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Just tired. Wiped out, really. I fell asleep on the sofa at seven o'clock last night, which isn't like me.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything when you stand up, or move around?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit dizzy when I get up quickly. It passes.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else you'd like to tell me?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Not really. I don't want to make a fuss.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): It isn't a fuss. Let me ask about a few specifics. Any bleeding, or pain in your tummy?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No, neither.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any burning when you pass water, or a fever?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): How about your breathing, any trouble there?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my breathing is fine.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your heart? Any trouble on that side?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing odd there either.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about your health in general. Any conditions, past or present?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got an underactive thyroid, and asthma since I was a kid. And anxiety, on and off. That's it.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking at the moment? Take your time.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Levothyroxine every morning on an empty stomach. The blue inhaler, salbutamol, when I need it. Folic acid once a day. And cyclizine from my GP for the sickness, 50 milligrams three times a day. I take it regularly.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She misses the lunchtime one most days, doctor. I've seen it sitting on the kitchen counter.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Sometimes I forget. It's not a big deal.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you both. Do you have any allergies?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none that I know of.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had any operations in the past?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): My appendix out, when I was fifteen.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does anything run in the family that I should know about?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Mum has thyroid problems, that's probably where mine comes from. And my sister was horribly sick in both her pregnancies.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's helpful to know. Do you smoke, or drink?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): I gave up smoking two years ago. And I haven't touched a drink since the test came back positive.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what do you do for work?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm a teaching assistant at a primary school. Which is fun, until the dinner smells hit at twelve.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): I can imagine. Right, I'm going to take a few measurements first, then I'll examine you.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is 112/70 mmHg. Pulse is 96 bpm. Temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius. Oxygen saturation 99 percent. And on the scales you are 61 kilograms.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that all right?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nothing alarming in those numbers. Now lie back for me, and let me feel your tummy. The abdomen is soft, and there is no tenderness anywhere.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Good.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, here is where I am. Sickness is very common in early pregnancy, but I can't rule out hyperemesis, the severe kind, given how often you are being sick.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. Is that likely?
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't know yet, which is why I'd like to do a few things today. A urine test, to look for ketones, and blood tests to check your salts and your kidneys. And I'll book an ultrasound scan to see how the pregnancy is getting on.
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Is the cyclizine all right for the baby?
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, it's one of the usual choices in pregnancy. Please carry on with it, and try to take the lunchtime dose as well.
[SEG0053] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll text her at twelve every day.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Dan, please.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's a perfectly good plan. Small meals, little and often, dry biscuits before you get out of bed, sips of fluid all day, and ginger if you like it. If you can't keep any fluids down for 24 hours, come back and see me that same day, don't wait.
[SEG0056] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. Thank you. I'm sure it'll settle by itself.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hope so. We'll see how you get on.
[SEG0058] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks, doctor.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so I kept a log. My right knee swelled up five days ago after a long day kneeling on a tile floor, and it hasn't gone down. I have the dates on my phone.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, thanks. Show me when you're ready. Is it only swollen, or is it painful too?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Painful, yes, it hurts in the knee. But I can't tell you when exactly the pain started. I wrote the swelling date, not the pain. I think the pain came first, maybe two days before. Maybe not.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's fine. Does it feel stiff?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Stiff after sitting in the truck, yes. Takes a minute to straighten.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it warm?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Warm to the touch, compared to the left. I checked with the back of my hand.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): And where does it hurt most?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Right at the front, over the kneecap. Tender when I press.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever, I took it last night.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Redness?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No redness.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does the knee lock?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No locking.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you fall or twist it?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No fall, no twist.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chills or sweats?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No chills.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medications are you taking?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen, maybe 400 mg, three times a day, for the knee. Metformin, 500 mg, twice a day, breakfast and dinner, though I skip some dinners. Lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day. And omeprazole, 20 mg, once a day.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any allergies?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Penicillin. My lips swelled up.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medical history?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Surgery?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Left knee scope in 2015. And a right shoulder surgery in 2019.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): My father has gout. My mother has arthritis.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Flooring installer, mostly tile. So a lot of kneeling.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Two beers after work, most days.
[SEG0034] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doc, the blood draw tray is ready whenever you want it. ~
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, give me five minutes. Let me check you. Temperature 37.9, blood pressure 132 over 84, pulse 84.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Is the temperature high? ~
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Slightly. Let me see the knee.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Careful. ~
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's swelling over the front of the right knee, like a bag of fluid in front of the kneecap.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): That's what I've been looking at. ~
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's warm, and tender over the kneecap itself. The knee still bends fully, though.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): It bends, yes. ~
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with your breathing, chest?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all, my chest is fine.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): This could be bursitis from kneeling, but I can't rule out an infection in the bursa, given the warmth and the temperature.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): Infection? From kneeling? ~
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): It happens when the skin gets broken. I'd like to arrange blood tests, including inflammation markers, and an X-ray of the knee.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can draw the bloods now, if you like. ~
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please. And I'd like to do an ultrasound of the knee, and I may need to draw some fluid out with a needle.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): Sounds unpleasant. ~
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's quick. Stop the ibuprofen on an empty stomach, and rest the knee, no kneeling for now.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): That's a week's pay gone. ~
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in two days.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Two days. I'll be here. ~

[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): It's just a smoker's cough. ~
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Frank, I'd like to hear it from you. Tell me about the morning cough.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): I cough when I get up. Bring up some phlegm. Then it's gone by mid-morning.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): What colour is the phlegm?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): White, mostly. A bit grey at times. ~
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many years has this been going on? ~
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Years. I can't say exactly. Ten, maybe. ~
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any breathlessness, or wheeze? ~
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Going up the stairs, I get puffed. But I'm fifty-eight. ~
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been puffed for a good while. ~
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much do you smoke?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Twenty a day. Since I was eighteen.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): A blue inhaler. Salbutamol. Two puffs, when I need it. Not often.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other conditions?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll listen to your chest. ~
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Go on.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's a bit of wheeze when you breathe out, and your breathing out takes longer than normal, otherwise clear.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi, doctor! I'm Priya, and I'm here for my epilepsy review, I've got so much to tell you, because I had a seizure, one, since my last visit, and I haven't stopped worrying about it.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you for telling me. When was the seizure?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Six weeks ago, on a Tuesday night. I was asleep, my husband woke up and I was shaking. It lasted about two minutes, he said.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How did you feel afterwards?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Awful. Confused, exhausted, a headache, and I'd bitten my tongue. I slept for twelve hours.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did anything seem to trigger it? ~
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I'd missed two doses of my tablet that week, and I'd had a few late nights. And a glass of wine. ~
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's an honest answer, thank you. Any other seizures, or odd episodes like staring or jerking?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None. Nothing else.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any injuries, falls, or fits during the day?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Lamotrigine, 150 mg, twice a day. I've been on it for four years.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any side effects, rashes, dizziness, double vision?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other conditions?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Epilepsy since I was fifteen. And I'm planning a pregnancy next year, that's partly why I came.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good thinking. Any operations?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): My appendix, when I was twenty.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check your reflexes and coordination, for completeness. ~
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Everything looks normal. Priya, a single seizure after missed doses and poor sleep isn't a failure of treatment. The tablet works, when it's taken regularly. ~
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): That's a relief. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to change the dose, but I'd like you to set a phone alarm for both doses, and use a weekly pill box.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll do both. ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep a regular sleep routine, limit alcohol, and avoid skipping meals.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): For your pregnancy plans, lamotrigine is one of the safer options, but you'll need folic acid at a higher dose before you conceive, 5 mg once a day.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Five milligrams. Okay. I'll start it. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please come and see me before you try, and tell the pharmacy you're planning a pregnancy.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep the driving restriction in mind, you must not drive for the period the rules set after a seizure. ~
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Understood. ~

[SEG0001] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, it's our son Rohan, he's three months old. He spits up after every single feed, and I'm worried he isn't keeping enough down.
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): Waaah. ~
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hello, little man. Thank you both for bringing him. Let me hear it from you first, Mum. How often does he spit up?
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): After every feed, doctor. Every single one.
[SEG0005] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That's not right. It's not every feed. Maybe one or two a day, and it's only a little.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is every feed, I do the night ones, you're asleep.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll note that you remember it differently, and we'll see how he looks. Is he feeding well otherwise?
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's hungry all the time. He takes about ninety millilitres, or maybe a hundred and twenty, I'm not sure. I don't measure carefully. ~
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's helpful. Is he bottle-fed or breast-fed? ~
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Formula only. We changed formula last month. ~
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Why did you change it?
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My sister says he's allergic to cow's milk formula, but I don't know what the reaction was.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I'll note that. Is he vomiting forcefully, or is it just milk coming up? ~
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just milk dribbling out, mostly. ~
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there any green or bloody vomit, or a swollen tummy?
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. None of that.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has he had any fever, or diarrhoea? ~
[SEG0018] person_4 (CAREGIVER): No, nothing like that. ~
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you been giving him, if anything?
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Colic drops, five drops with each feed, I think.
[SEG0021] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She gives them, but I forget half the time when I do the evening feed.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you for being honest. I'll weigh him and check his temperature. ~
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been gaining, the health visitor said so. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight 6.2 kilograms, temperature 36.7.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that good? ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's a healthy weight for three months. Let me feel his tummy and look at him. ~
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Of course.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): His tummy is soft, no lumps, and he looks well.
[SEG0029] person_4 (CAREGIVER): So he's fine? ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): He seems well, and growing well. This sounds like reflux, which is very common at this age, and he's not showing any warning signs.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What can we do? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to start a sachet of infant Gaviscon, one sachet with each feed, mixed in the milk.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the drops? ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): We can stop those for now. Keep him upright for twenty minutes after each feed, and try smaller, more frequent feeds.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll do the evening ones properly. ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in three weeks, or sooner if he vomits forcefully, goes green, or stops feeding.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will. Thank you. ~

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you get a new headache, jaw pain or changes to your vision, call us the same day.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. ~

[SEG0001] person_4 (NURSE): Dr Hughes, this is Arlo, he's five, and his mum is here about his snoring. I'll leave you to it. ~
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, nurse. Hello Arlo, hello Mum. What's been going on? ~
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He snores. Properly, like a lorry. It's been about a year, getting worse.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't snore. ~
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You do, sweetheart. I recorded it, I've got it on my phone. ~
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Could I hear a bit of it? ~
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Of course. Here you go. ~
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Goodness. That's loud. Does he stop breathing at all, in the night?
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sometimes it sounds like he pauses. Not for long. A few seconds.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does he have a fever at the moment?
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No fever, no.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble swallowing?
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): None, he eats like a horse.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And during the day, how's he? ~
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A bit cranky by the afternoon. He used to nap, and he doesn't now. ~
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And does he ever wake up grumpy or tired? ~
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, he's often grumpy first thing. ~
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there a history of tonsil problems, Mum?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's had tonsillitis twice, last year.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where's he at in school?
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Reception, at the village primary.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arlo, can you open your mouth wide like a lion? ~
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Roar! ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Perfect. Can you do it again? ~
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Roar! ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, I can see. Mum, I'm going to explain what I'm looking for. Tonsils sit at the back of the throat. In some children, they are very big. ~
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Are his big? ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll tell you after I've explained what the options are. Sometimes big tonsils can narrow the airway at night. ~
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that what's causing the snoring? ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): It might be. I won't put a label on it today. I'd like to arrange an overnight oxygen level test at home, so we can see how he breathes while he sleeps.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): How does that work? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): A small sensor goes on his toe, and it records through the night. The nurse will give you the kit. ~
[SEG0033] person_4 (NURSE): I'll get it ready for you, Mrs Webb. ~
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And then? ~
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we'll know whether it's a simple snore or whether it affects his sleep. ~
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That makes sense. Thank you. ~
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arlo, you were a very good lion. ~
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Rrrr! ~

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it Siobhan Brennan? Siobhan, with the two b's? ~
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): That's me, doctor, one b and two n's, but sure, you're close enough. Isn't it a grand morning for a broken wrist!
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ha. So, this is your fracture clinic check, the cast comes off next week. How's it been going? ~
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Grand, mostly. It was my own fault, I came off the bike on the Phoenix Park road, hit a pothole, my husband never lets me forget it. Five weeks ago now.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Five weeks. Any itching under the cast?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Desperately. I've been poking a knitting needle down it, don't tell the nurse.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): I won't. Any swelling in the fingers?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit in the evenings, they feel fat, like sausages.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are the fingers stiff?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Very. I can barely make a fist.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any aching at night?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): In the wrist, yes, when I lie on it.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness in the hand?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No numbness.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pins and needles?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any sores, or rubbing under the edge of the cast?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No sores. I looked with a torch.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any smell coming from it?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No smell. I put my nose right up to it.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Paracetamol, maybe 1 gram, when it's sore. And a big white chewy tablet for the bones, I don't know what it's called, my mother takes the same one. And omeprazole, 20 mg, in the morning.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll find the chewable on your record. Any allergies?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): None at all. No allergies.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medical history?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit of thin bones, osteopenia, and acid reflux.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): A caesarean, in 2015.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bone problems in the family?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother has osteoporosis.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Primary school teacher. Thirty small children and one broken wrist, you can imagine.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the cycling, how often?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Three times a week, before this.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Blood pressure 124 over 76, pulse 70.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that all right? ~
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Perfect. Let me look at the cast.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Be gentle. ~
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): The cast is intact and dry, no cracks.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): I've been very careful in the shower. ~
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the fingers are warm, pink, with good colour.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): They're a bit puffy. ~
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wiggle them for me. I can see you move all five fingers well.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): There, like a pianist. ~
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any problem with feeling in your hand?
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing, it's all normal.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any problem with your breathing?
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Here's what I think. The fracture is healing well so far, from how it looks and feels.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): That's great. ~
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Next week, before the cast comes off, I'd like to arrange an X-ray of the wrist, to see the bone.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): That's what I was hoping. ~
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Given your thin bones and family history, I'd also like to arrange a bone density scan, and a vitamin D blood test.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Goodness, the full works. ~
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Better to be thorough. I'd like to see you again next week to take the cast off.
[SEG0056] person_1 (PATIENT): Next week. I'll bring a cake. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I have no complaints at all, I'm here for my annual health check, and I'd like blood tests, as I've read it's sensible after forty.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): It is sensible. Let me start with some questions. How are you in yourself? ~
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Very well, honestly. A few small things. I sometimes get mild heartburn after spicy food.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How often?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Perhaps once a week.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): My lower back is a little stiff when I wake up. It goes after a shower.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Energy levels?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. A bit tired by the evening, but I work long hours.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No chest pain.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you take at the moment?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): A multivitamin, a little yellow capsule, from the pharmacy. I forget its name. And vitamin C, maybe 500 mg, once a day.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. And what do you do for a living?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm a software architect. Desk-bound, I'm afraid.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me take your numbers. Blood pressure 126 over 78, pulse 68, weight 72 kilos.
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): That's good, isn't it? ~
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Very good. I'm going to feel your tummy.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Go ahead. ~
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your abdomen is soft and not tender.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Good. ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the muscles of your lower back are a bit tight on both sides.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): That's the stiffness. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Overall you're in good shape. I think you're healthy for your age, with only minor, easily managed complaints.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): That's what I hoped. ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): For the heartburn, I'd like to start omeprazole, 20 mg, once a day, before breakfast.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): For how long? ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): A month, and we'll see. And for the back, I'd suggest paracetamol, 1 gram, when it's stiff.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I rarely take anything. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Only when you need it. Now the tests. I'd like to arrange a full blood count with liver and kidney function, and a cholesterol and HbA1c test.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Do I need to fast? ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): For the cholesterol, yes, from midnight. Water is fine. ~
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): And stretch your back for a few minutes each morning.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll do that. ~
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the heartburn isn't better in four weeks, come back and see me.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Four weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hi, doctor. I'm Tanya, Zoe's mum, and this is Nan, my mum, who looks after Zoe after school. Zoe's got her mock exams, and she's been in a state. ~
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hi, Zoe. Do you want to tell me, or would you rather Mum starts? ~
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Mum. ~
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been getting these awful butterflies, and her heart races before every exam, and she's been waking up at three in the morning going over things.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Zoe, is that how it feels to you?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah. ~
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Dunno. Term two? Maybe?
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It was before Christmas, love.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I thought it was after the first mock. I can't be sure.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. What about sleep?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Bad.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything running in the family, anxiety, worrying?
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Me, yes, her mum. I was anxious as a teenager.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): What year are you in, Zoe?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Twelve.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): And outside school, what do you do?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Swim. Mornings.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Pulse 96, blood pressure 112 over 70.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's a bit fast, isn't it? ~
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Slightly, she's nervous being here. Zoe, show me your hands?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): They're always sweaty. ~
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your hands are cool and a bit clammy.
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Gross. ~
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Here's what I think. This looks like exam anxiety, and it's very common at this age.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is it serious? ~
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not dangerous, but it's making life hard, and it's worth helping. ~
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): What can we do? ~
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): A few things. For the nights, I'd like to start melatonin, 2 mg, half an hour before bed.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is it safe for her age? ~
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): For short use, yes, and I'll review it. And for the exam days, I'd like to give propranolol, 10 mg, to take an hour before an exam, only on those days.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Will it make her drowsy? ~
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not usually. It calms the shaky, racing feeling. Zoe, you can try it on a practice day first. ~
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): And slow breathing helps. In for four, hold for four, out for six.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I do that already. ~
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep going, and cut caffeine after lunchtime.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Energy drinks? ~
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Those too. ~
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. ~
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in three weeks, before the real exams.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hi, doctor. This is Oscar, he's seven. His eczema's flared, and I'm worried about the steroid cream, I've read it thins the skin, and I'm not sure we should keep using it.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understandable. Oscar, where's the itchiest bit?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Elbows. And behind the knees.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is your skin dry?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Very.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it keep you awake?
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He scratches in his sleep, he wakes up crying.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weeping or crusting?
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing wet.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you using?
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hydrocortisone cream, once a day, on the red bits. And cetirizine syrup.
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): I have 5 ml.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's 10 ml, Oscar. I measure it.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll check the label. Oscar, any allergies? Anything you can't eat?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm not allergic to anything.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, the egg, last year, he came up in hives, I'm not sure it was an allergy though.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record both. Any other history?
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just the eczema, since a baby.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): And school?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Year two.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swimming?
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Lessons on Saturday. The chlorine stings him.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check him. Temperature 36.7, pulse 90, breathing 20, oxygen 99 percent, weight 24 kilos, height 120 centimetres.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): All fine? ~
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): All good. Oscar, show me your elbows.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Here. ~
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dry, red, scaly patches in both elbow creases and behind the knees.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's what I see. ~
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And some scratch marks, but no sign of crusting.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Good. ~
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze or cough?
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing at all.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like an eczema flare, but I can't rule out a skin infection on top, so I'd like to arrange a skin swab.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is the steroid cream safe? ~
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Used the way I describe, yes. Short bursts on red areas only, thinning happens with long, heavy use.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's reassuring. ~
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Moisturise generously, several times a day.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Will do. ~
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again in two weeks.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two weeks. Thank you. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, you're alright, take a seat. What can I do for you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Uh, you know, hello, doctor, I came in with them, if that's okay.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, it's a red warm patch on my shin. That's what we're worried about.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many days or weeks has it been?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): I mean, it's been about a month, I'm fairly sure.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much does it limit you?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, it feels moderate to me.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, any other symptoms with it?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Erm, when it starts I tend to get a sore leg as well.
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): And the other thing I wanted to mention is that I can't really—
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell the doctor about the other thing, that's what worries me.
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): I, I was getting to that! The sore leg? That's been for about four days.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse.
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I notice it more with walking. It's moderate, honestly.
[SEG0016] person_5 (UNKNOWN): Mm, that's what happened, yes.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what about cut or rash elsewhere?

[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath?

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood. Any breathing difficulties apart from this?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No problems with breathing.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): What line of work are you in?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm a bus driver, so I sit for long hours.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): What does a normal day of food look like?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Lots of rice, lentils and some fruit.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any past operations I should know about?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Just my septum straightened, in my thirties.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, before we go further, any allergies?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Actually, no, nothing as far as I know.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Actually, I remember she had some kind of reaction to amoxicillin before. I couldn't swear to it.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Maybe, but I don't recall it.

[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Actually, you know, doctor, I think the last prescription for the gliclazide was 40 milligrams. We changed it at the last visit.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, I see. Is the most recent prescription on you?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I left it at home.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): What conditions have you been treated for in the past?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah, I've got low haemoglobin. I've never really been one for hospitals.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, what else?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): I have eczema.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah, I've had an underactive thyroid, yes. I have diabetes.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, low haemoglobin is known to us, good to have that clear.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any inherited conditions that you know of in the family?
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so my aunt has rheumatoid arthritis. Ah, my brother has epilepsy.
[SEG0048] person_6 (NURSE): Here are the numbers, doctor. Temp 38.6 degrees, oxygen saturation is 96 percent. BMI works out to 32.5, height 155 centimetres, weight 78 kilos, respiratory rate 18, pressure 110 over 66, pulse 101.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, noted.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at the area, I'll be gentle.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Look straight ahead.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): The shin is red, warm and tender with a clear edge, and I've marked it with a pen.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please sit back down. Okay, so my impression is this: The most likely explanation is cellulitis of the leg. We shouldn't forget a blood clot in the leg. Just to be sure I understood. You've had a red warm patch on your shin for about a month, moderate, and no rash elsewhere or cut.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, you've got it.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood tests is what I'd like next, for cellulitis. The result will help us decide whether anything more is needed. Keep the leg raised and come back if the redness goes past the pen line. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose.
[SEG0056] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright, I follow.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): The thing that would worry me is if the symptoms get worse. If that happens, go to emergency. I'd like you back in two days.

[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell the doctor about the other thing, that's what worries me.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, diabetes is known to us, good to have that clear. Do you do any exercise?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I swim twice a week.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep windows closed on high-pollen days and wash your hair at night. Is there anything you'd like me to go over again?

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi, doctor, I came as soon as they called me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem at all, come in. What's troubling you?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I wanted to get painful periods looked at.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When was the first time you noticed it?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Ever since... since yesterday, really.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood. Can you describe it a bit more for me? How strong it is, what the pattern is, what helps.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I notice it more with first two days. I'd say a few times a day.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you noticed anything else alongside it?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): A dull ache in my back goes along with it, most of the time.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had painful periods before, or is this the first time?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit, about six months ago. It settled by itself back then.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What operations have you had, if any?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): I had a bunion operation six years ago.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's on your current medicine list?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Losartan. I take it 50 milligrams, once a day. I'm on ibuprofen, with food when needed.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what strength is that?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): It's 400 milligrams.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you got any known allergies?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing as far as I know.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about any past illnesses or ongoing conditions.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I've had high blood pressure for about a year now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other things?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I have gout, for two years.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so high blood pressure is already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today. Anything you do to stay fit?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I do a yoga class on Thursdays.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you live by yourself?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I share a house with my brother.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are your meals?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I grab fast food at lunch most days.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had any pain with sex?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Not that I've noticed, no pain with sex.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you get bleeding between periods, fever or heavy bleeding?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No, not a single one.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, any breathing difficulties apart from this?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): No problems with breathing.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can I check a few measurements before we carry on?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's it, just a little longer...
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: saturation 98 percent, BP is 119 over 77. And respiratory rate 15, temp 36.6 degrees, pulse is 82 beats a minute.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll examine you in a second, make yourself comfortable.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel here.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is soft and not tender between periods.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, you can get dressed.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me and what I found, this looks most like primary dysmenorrhoea. Heat, gentle exercise, and start the tablet at the first sign of pain. Does all of that make sense?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): I think I understand everything. Thanks.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): All the best.

[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): It happens all the time.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you noticed heavy bleeding, bleeding between periods or pain with sex?

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at the area, I'll be gentle.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hold that for a second.

[SEG0005] person_4 (PATIENT): I wanted to get tiredness looked at.

[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had tiredness before, or is this the first time?
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, something like this happened a couple of years ago, and it went away on its own.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): What operations have you had, if any?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, I had a caesarean for my second baby, nine years ago.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before we go further, any allergies?
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): No, I've never reacted to anything.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who lives with you?
[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): My partner and our baby.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's your work?
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): I'm a plumber, lots of bending and kneeling.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you take any prescribed or over-the-counter medicines?
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She is on omeprazole, 20 milligrams, once a day, I give it to her. She takes sertraline, 50 milligrams, once a day. It's propranolol, 40 milligrams, twice a day, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your medical history?
[SEG0024] person_4 (PATIENT): Acid reflux, for about ten years.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah.

[SEG0028] person_4 (PATIENT): I haven't had joint pain or vomiting, no.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you get weight loss or fever?
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): No, I haven't had any of them.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any problems with your joints or muscles?
[SEG0032] person_4 (PATIENT): I move fine otherwise.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your breathing, any trouble there?

[SEG0040] person_4 (PATIENT): Good, thanks, I'll see you then.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Goodbye for now.

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Look after yourself.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order a urine protein test, for pre-eclampsia.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Book a review straight away.

[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else on your mind before you go?
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): That's clear, thanks.
